text:
anya: Quick sync — after the anchor swap yesterday, q4b-int8 shows a cluster of low-quality outputs on the 'convo-summarize' promptset. Not huge volume but concentrated in a few paraphrase families. Flagging for curation + relabel plan. :eyes:
kevin: Can you drop one or two concrete examples of the failure modes? helps me triage if it's model hallucination vs tokenization drift.
anya: Sure — examples below (shortened):
```
prompt: "Summarize the customer's last three messages about billing and refunds."
gold: "Customer asked about pro-rata refunds and disputed charges; recommended refund and escalate to billing ops."
q4b-int8: "They want to cancel. Offer discount."
notes: wrong intent, dropped context, hallucinated offer.
```
kevin: ack. that looks like context clipping + a hallucinated action. curious if this correlates with long-prefix KV cache expiry after anchor change.
sophia: We also saw higher token-break differences in the same families — tokenizer split differences after anchor re-token mapping. Attached a quick stat: TOKEN_BREAK_RATE up ~1.7% on sampled prompts.
anya: tagging @labeler-bot — can you queue a focused relabel job for the 300 most-ambiguous paraphrase clusters from that seed? Prefer human review + second-pass adjudication.
labeler-bot: queued 312 items to curation-miniholdout-2026-03; expected throughput 24/hr; estimated completion 13h.
james: For dedupe: suggest we run a soft similarity sweep first (threshold 0.82) to collapse near-duplicates but keep paraphrase variance for eval. Command I'm thinking: `python infra/dedupe/runner.py --mode soft --threshold 0.82 --anchor-set convo-summarize-seed`
oliver: I'll run that dedupe locally and push the candidate mappings to staging. Also propose we freeze the mini-holdout (the golden subset used for canary) during the relabel window so evals are stable.
anya: Yes freeze + snapshot. After relabel we run a before/after microbench: 1) full pass on frozen mini-holdout 2) new labels applied 3) compare precision/recall and per-intent confusion. If delta > 3% on intent F1 we halt rollout.
sophia: Also recommending a lightweight tokenizer remap check: run the token-split diff on the changed anchors and filter prompts where split_count delta > 2. Those are the highest risk.
kevin: Good. Can we add a small smoke harness to fail fast in CI for this model variant? Something like: if mini-holdout intent-F1 drops more than 2.5% and hallucination rate increases > 1.0% then mark as unstable. I can sketch the CI check.
anya: Perfect — Kevin, can you own the CI guard? James/Oliver handle dedupe + push candidates; Labeler-bot + human labelers do relabel and adjudication; Sophia to run tokenizer diagnostics. I'll coordinate with product to hold the canary for 24h.
james: will do dedupe run now, will post diffs and a CSV of cluster heads to this thread.
oliver: started dedupe, ETA 40m. posting preliminary clusters as soon as ready. :thumbsup:
labeler-bot: progress update: 48 labeled, 0 adjudicated so far.
anya: thanks all. If anyone spots a systemic pattern (same hallucinated phrase across many samples) call it out — could be a model artifact we want to mitigate via prompt sanitization or prefix-preservation.
sophia: noted — I'll also surface a tiny script to normalize punctuation that seems to change tokenization: `scripts/normalize_punct.py --in X --out Y` and run on the flagged subset.
kevin: adding a tiny note here: when we swap anchors next time we should run a back-compat cluster diff to anticipate these collisions. created a tiny ticket: PS-anch-swap-diff.
anya: great. leaving this thread as the coordination point — will post the final relabel summary and follow-up checklist once adjudication completes. :white_check_mark:
